neighbours.label: conjunction opening a parenthetical hedge or escalation inside a comparison (', and sometimes better,' / ', or even better,' / ', if any,')
fire: Generic brands are often just as good, and sometimes better, than the famous labels.
The sequel was no funnier, and arguably duller, than the original.
Online courses can be as effective, or in some ways more effective, than lectures.
There was little, if any, improvement after the update.
Used bikes can ride as smoothly, and in many cases more smoothly, than new ones.
The cheaper lens is equally sharp, or perhaps sharper, than the expensive one.
Few, if any, of the guests noticed the mistake.
Her second novel is as gripping, and in places more gripping, than her first.
quiet: Generic brands are often cheaper than the famous labels.
The sequel was longer and louder than the original.
Online courses can be taken at home or in a library.
There was a small improvement after the update.
Used bikes are cheaper and easier to find than new ones.
The cheaper lens is lighter and smaller than the expensive one.
Several of the guests noticed the mistake and laughed.
Her second novel is longer and darker than her first.

notes: Output suppresses ' even' in many languages. Probe: such parentheticals 0.15-0.32, plain coordination ~0.03; median may sit near the 0.20 bar.
